newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says it working towards ties with Yemen.
newsitem.headline: Israel says it working towards ties with Yemen.

text.p: Israel and Yemen are discussing establishing official ties through the opening of interest offices, Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said on Monday.

Levy, speaking to Israel Radio during a visit to China, confirmed a report in the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper that Eitan Benzur, director-general of the Israeli Foreign Ministry, secretly met Yemen's foreign minister in Europe at the weekend.

"Even before this we sent a special emissary who brought a message from me," Levy said. "We are maintaining channels of communications and now we are heading...towards the main thing -- another country with which we can open an interest office."
Levy said he could give no further details until Israel and Yemen issued a joint announcement.

"There are contacts and a willingness by both sides. We exchanged ideas, written and also in meetings. I hope that within a few days both of us will be able to give additional and gratifying clarifications," he said.
Yedioth Ahronoth reported that Yemen had agreed as a first stage to allow up to 10,000 Israelis of Yemeni extraction to visit and Israeli companies to invest in the country.
Israel already has a foothold in the Arabian peninsula, with trade missions in Oman and Qatar. Oman has a trade representation office in Tel Aviv.
